resolution.note: The launcher polls herdr agent get on the new pane (1 s interval, 60 s default, --start-seconds) and prints success and renames the predecessor tab only once Herdr shows claude or codex (any agent for an override); otherwise it exits 1 naming the pane and keeps the tab. Live probe from a scratch pane: successor: herdr tab w1D:tAR pane w1D:pAX agent claude unknown, exit 0 within 3 s. Verbatim Codex capture agent-get-idle-codex.reply.jsonl. Follow-up t-g1cwxm2: a successor blocked on a startup dialog.

title: Confirm the successor agent started before the launcher reports success
body:
Outcome: scripts/claude/successor-launch.ts prints success and renames the predecessor tab only after Herdr shows the expected agent in the new pane; a successor that never started fails the launch and names the pane.
Evidence: the official herdr skill (herdrdev/herdr skills/herdr/SKILL.md, v0.9.5 line 189) says `pane run` success "acknowledges admission, not command execution", yet the launcher treats exit 0 of `herdr pane run` as started (also recorded in t-14b4ab6, closed as a duplicate without this fix). The official `agent start` is not a drop-in (t-tdkpgag): it rejects any argument with a control character (src/app/agents.rs), needs a unique [a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31} name, starts Herdr's canonical executable instead of KRN_SUCCESSOR_AGENT, fails with agent_not_ready on a startup dialog while the agent is live, and its reply cannot be captured without creating a pane. Poll `herdr agent get <new pane>` for the expected agent instead (read-only; verbatim captures in test/fixtures/herdr).
Proof: a test with the verbatim agent get captures where the new pane reports no agent until a deadline fails the launch, leaves the predecessor tab name alone and exits non-zero; the lead runs one live launch in a scratch pane and sees the poll report a started Claude.
